documents.title: Office Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Routine BP/GERD check. No complaints. Work picking back up after winter. Takes both meds daily, no side effects he notices. No heartburn breakthrough.

Exam: BP as charted, his usual range. Heart RRR. Lungs clear. No ankle swelling.

A/P: HTN stable on HCTZ 25, continue; BMP. GERD stable on omeprazole 20, continue. Physical in October; at 45 we'll start colon cancer screening, he'd rather do the stool kit than a colonoscopy.

documents.title: Refills
documents.author: patient
documents.body: Hey, pharmacy says I'm out of refills on both the blood pressure pill and the stomach one. Can you send new ones? Same place as before. Thanks, Derek

documents.title: RE: Refills
documents.author: RN
documents.body: Hi Derek, both are in: hydrochlorothiazide 25 mg and omeprazole 20 mg, 90 days each with refills through your next physical. Should be ready later today.

documents.title: Annual Physical
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
45M for yearly exam. Feels good, no new issues. Keeping up at work without trouble. No chest pain, palpitations, or breathing complaints. Bowels regular, no blood. Reflux controlled on omeprazole. Five years off cigarettes.

Meds: HCTZ 25 daily, omeprazole 20 daily. NKDA.

Exam: vitals as charted. Alert, comfortable. Eyes and ears normal. No lymphadenopathy. Heart regular rate and rhythm. Lungs clear to auscultation, no crackles. Abdomen soft and nontender. Extremities warm, no edema. Neuro grossly intact.

A/P:
1. HTN: at his usual, continue HCTZ. CMP.
2. GERD: continue omeprazole.
3. Colorectal screening, average risk, age 45: FIT kit handed to him, mail it back this week.
4. Labs: CBC, lipids, A1c.
5. Flu and updated Pfizer COVID given in clinic.
Next routine visit in the spring.

documents.title: FIT Result
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: FIT negative. Repeat yearly. Portal note sent.

documents.title: Breathing
documents.author: patient
documents.body: Morning. For about two months I've been getting winded way easier than normal, carrying stuff up ladders or stairs, and I've got this dry cough that won't quit. No fever. Figured it was a winter thing but it's not going away. Can I come in?

documents.title: RE: Breathing
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Glad you wrote. I'd like to listen to you and get some tests. Front desk will put you in Monday 2/19 at 10:30. If you get short of breath at rest, chest pain, or lips turning blue before then, go to the ER.

reports.text:
Clinical indication: two months of exertional dyspnea and dry cough. Former smoker.
Comparison: none available.
PA and lateral views of the chest. Reticular opacities are present in both lungs, more pronounced in the lower lobes. No focal consolidation. No pleural effusion or pneumothorax. Heart size normal. Mediastinal contours unremarkable. Osseous structures intact.
reports.conclusion: Bilateral reticular opacities with lower-lobe predominance, suggesting interstitial lung disease. Recommend high-resolution CT for further characterization.

orders.reason: Reticular opacities on chest x-ray, exertional dyspnea

procedures.procedure: Office visit, established patient, moderate MDM

documents.title: Office Visit: Dyspnea and Cough
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
S: 45M with HTN and GERD. Since around mid-December he gets out of breath with exertion that never used to bother him: ladders, hauling material, two flights of stairs. Slowly worse. Dry cough, no sputum, no blood. No fever, chills or night sweats. Hasn't traveled, nobody sick at home or on the crew. No chest pain or palpitations, no leg swelling, no orthopnea. Reflux controlled. Never had lung trouble before, no asthma. Quit smoking 2018, 30 pack-years. Meds unchanged: HCTZ 25, omeprazole 20. NKDA.

O: BP 135/85, HR 88, RR 20, SpO2 94% on room air (has been 97-98 here). Comfortable sitting, speaks full sentences. No JVD. Heart regular, no murmur or gallop. Lungs: fine inspiratory crackles at both bases, no wheeze. No clubbing. No calf tenderness, no edema.

CXR in office: reticular opacities both lungs, lower zones worse.

A/P: Exertional dyspnea and dry cough with bibasilar crackles, borderline resting sat, and an interstitial pattern on x-ray. Worried about an interstitial lung disease rather than infection or heart failure. Ex-smoker, so differential includes smoking-related ILD; also checking for a connective tissue cause.
- HRCT chest, ordered today, try to get it this week.
- CBC, BMP, ESR, ANA, RF today.
- Pulmonology referral once CT is back.
- Return precautions reviewed: worsening breathlessness, chest pain, fever, go to the ED.

documents.title: Blood Work
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Derek, Monday's labs: blood counts normal, kidney function normal (creatinine 0.9), inflammation marker (ESR) 20, which is okay, and the two autoimmune screens (ANA and rheumatoid factor) were negative. That makes a rheumatologic cause less likely. CT is tomorrow morning, I'll call you when I have the read.

reports.text:
Technique: high-resolution non-contrast CT of the chest with thin-section inspiratory, expiratory and prone images.
Comparison: chest radiograph 2024-02-19.
Findings: Bilateral subpleural honeycombing with traction bronchiectasis. No consolidation or ground-glass predominance. No pulmonary mass or suspicious nodule. Airways otherwise patent. No pleural effusion. No mediastinal or hilar lymphadenopathy. Heart size normal, no pericardial effusion. Thoracic aorta normal caliber. Limited upper abdomen unremarkable.
reports.conclusion: Subpleural honeycombing and traction bronchiectasis, in keeping with established pulmonary fibrosis. Clinical and pulmonology correlation recommended.

orders.reason: Pulmonary fibrosis on HRCT, exertional dyspnea

conditions.label: Idiopathic pulmonary fibrosis
conditions.note: HRCT honeycombing and traction bronchiectasis; ANA and RF negative; pulmonology to confirm

documents.title: HRCT Result Call
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Called Derek with the CT. Shows scarring at the edges of both lungs with honeycombing and pulled-open airways, which fits pulmonary fibrosis. With negative ANA/RF and no other explanation found, the leading concern is idiopathic pulmonary fibrosis. Added to problem list pending pulmonology. Explained this is a chronic condition, that there are medicines that slow it, and that a lung specialist will confirm and plan treatment. He took it quietly, asked good questions. Urgent pulmonology referral placed. He has my cell.

documents.title: Referral Scheduled
documents.author: front desk
documents.body: Pulmonology referral faxed with CXR, HRCT report and labs. Their first new-patient opening is Tue 4/16. Pt aware and okay with date, will call if anything worsens. Asked them to put him on the cancellation list.

reports.text: Full pulmonary function testing: spirometry, lung volumes and diffusing capacity. Acceptable and reproducible efforts. FVC 70% predicted. DLCO 55% predicted.
reports.conclusion: Reduced FVC with reduced diffusing capacity, consistent with fibrotic lung disease.

medications.sig: Take 1 capsule by mouth twice daily with food, about 12 hours apart

documents.title: Pulmonology Consultation
documents.author: pulmonology
documents.body:
Pulmonary Medicine Consultation
Date of service: 04/16/2024
Referring: primary care physician
Reason: interstitial changes on imaging, exertional dyspnea

Thank you for asking us to see Mr. Mayhew, a 46-year-old construction worker with hypertension and GERD. He comes to us to continue the evaluation you began in February of breathlessness on exertion and a dry cough, now about four months in total. He reports no chest pain, fevers or weight loss. He is a former smoker of 30 pack-years who stopped in 2018. No family history of fibrotic lung disease. No pets or birds at home, no hobbies with organic dust.

Medications: hydrochlorothiazide 25 mg daily, omeprazole 20 mg daily.
Allergies: no known drug allergies.
Surgical history: tonsillectomy in childhood.
Family history: father with hypertension (72), mother with type 2 diabetes (75).

Examination: BP 135/85, HR 78, SpO2 94% on room air at rest. Bibasilar inspiratory crackles. No digital clubbing. No peripheral edema. Cardiac exam normal.

Data reviewed: February labs with hemoglobin 14.5, WBC 7,000, platelets 250,000, creatinine 0.9, ANA negative, RF negative. We reviewed the February HRCT images directly: bilateral, subpleural, basal-predominant reticular abnormality with minimal honeycombing.
Pulmonary function testing today: FVC 70% predicted, DLCO 55% predicted.

Impression: Idiopathic pulmonary fibrosis. The imaging pattern is typical, serologies are negative and we find no exposure or drug to account for it, so we are comfortable with the diagnosis without biopsy.

Plan:
1. Antifibrotic therapy: we discussed both available agents and he chose nintedanib 150 mg by mouth twice daily with food. Sent to the specialty pharmacy. Common GI effects reviewed.
2. Liver tests at 1 month and then every 3 months while on treatment; we will order and follow these.
3. Continue omeprazole for reflux.
4. Pneumococcal and yearly influenza vaccination recommended; we defer to you.
5. Follow-up here in about 6 weeks with labs.

Sincerely,
Pulmonary Medicine

documents.title: Office Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Here to go over the lung specialist visit. Pulmonology confirmed IPF (letter 4/23 reviewed with him) and started nintedanib 150 mg twice daily about four weeks ago, through the specialty pharmacy. Taking it with breakfast and dinner, managing so far. Still short of breath on hills and ladders, about the same as February, dry cough persists. Still working, foreman is letting him take more of the layout work.

Vitals as charted, SpO2 94% RA. Bibasilar crackles, unchanged. Heart regular. No edema.

A/P:
1. IPF on nintedanib, followed by pulmonology, who are doing the liver tests. Nintedanib added to our med list.
2. HTN at his baseline, continue HCTZ 25.
3. GERD, continue omeprazole 20; relevant to the lungs too.
4. Chronic lung disease: PCV20 given today. Flu and COVID in the fall.
See him for his physical in the fall.

documents.title: Outside Lab: Hepatic Panel
documents.author: RN
documents.body: Hepatic panel ordered by pulmonology (one month on nintedanib), copy received. All values in range. Scanned and filed.

reports.text: PA and lateral chest. Bilateral interstitial infiltrates. No focal consolidation, effusion or pneumothorax. Normal heart size. No mass.
reports.conclusion: Bilateral interstitial infiltrates consistent with known interstitial lung disease.

reports.text: High-resolution non-contrast CT of the chest. Comparison 2024-02-22. Interstitial lung disease as previously described. No pulmonary mass or suspicious nodule. No pleural effusion. No mediastinal or hilar lymphadenopathy. Heart normal in size.
reports.conclusion: Interstitial lung disease, confirmed. No mass or nodule.

reports.text: Spirometry, lung volumes and diffusing capacity. Restrictive pattern. Reduced diffusing capacity.
reports.conclusion: Restrictive ventilatory defect with reduced diffusion capacity.

documents.title: Pulmonology Follow-up
documents.author: pulmonology
documents.body:
Pulmonary Medicine Follow-up
Date of service: 06/03/2024

Mr. Mayhew returns for idiopathic pulmonary fibrosis, previously seen here in April after your evaluation in February. For the past two weeks his exertional breathlessness and dry cough have been a bit worse. He is concerned about lung cancer because of his smoking history and asked us directly how likely that is given his symptoms and tests.

Medications: nintedanib 150 mg twice daily, hydrochlorothiazide 25 mg daily, omeprazole 20 mg daily. No known drug allergies.
Past history: hypertension, GERD. Tonsillectomy as a child. 30 pack-years, quit 2018.

Exam: BP 135/85, HR 88, RR 20, SpO2 94% on room air. Inspiratory crackles at both bases.

Results today: hemoglobin 14.5, WBC 7,000, platelets 250,000; sodium 140, potassium 4.2, creatinine 1.0, calcium 9.8, liver enzymes normal. CEA within normal limits. ANA and RF negative previously.
Chest x-ray: bilateral interstitial infiltrates.
HRCT: interstitial lung disease as before; no mass or nodule.
PFTs: restrictive pattern with reduced diffusion capacity.

Assessment and plan:
1. IPF on nintedanib, tolerating it with normal liver tests. Continue.
2. Cancer concern: we went through his scan with him. There is no mass or nodule, and his marker is normal; nothing here points to lung cancer. He was visibly relieved.
3. Continue reflux treatment.
4. Liver tests every 3 months; return in about 8 months with repeat imaging and PFTs, sooner for any change.

Pulmonary Medicine

documents.title: Lung Doctor
documents.author: patient
documents.body: Saw the lung doctor last week. They said no sign of cancer on the scan which honestly was what I was losing sleep over. Staying on the nintedanib. Just wanted you to know.

documents.title: RE: Lung Doctor
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Thanks for letting me know, Derek. I got their letter yesterday and read it. Very good news on the scan. Keep taking the nintedanib, and reach out any time the breathing changes.

documents.title: Refill: Hydrochlorothiazide
documents.author: RN
documents.body: HCTZ 25 mg #90 requested. Last BMP in June via pulmonology, potassium 4.2, creatinine 1.0. Approved with 1 refill.

documents.title: Annual Physical
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Yearly physical, 46M. IPF diagnosed this year, on nintedanib through pulmonology since April, liver tests normal on their monitoring. Breathing on exertion about where it was in the summer; still working, mostly lighter tasks. Dry cough persists. Mood okay, PHQ-2 1. Off cigarettes six years.

Meds: nintedanib 150 mg BID, HCTZ 25 mg daily, omeprazole 20 mg daily. NKDA.

Exam: vitals as charted, SpO2 94% RA. Well appearing, no distress. HEENT normal. Neck supple. Heart regular, no murmur. Lungs: bibasilar inspiratory crackles as before. Abdomen benign. No clubbing, no edema.

A/P:
1. IPF: stable by his account, pulmonology follow-up early next year.
2. HTN: continue HCTZ. CMP.
3. GERD: continue omeprazole.
4. Health maintenance: lipids, A1c. FIT kit given. Flu and updated COVID given today; PCV20 done in May.
Recheck in the spring after his pulmonology visit.

documents.body: Negative FIT. Physical labs also normal. Patient notified through the portal. Next FIT fall 2025.
